headline: Forecasters are confident a significant storm brings a cold, rainy and windy stretch from Wednesday afternoon through at least Thanksgiving morning, with several inches of rain likely and gusts of 30 to 40 mph (possibly 40 to 50 mph) that could cause isolated power outages around Charlotte and the region.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Tuesday stays dry around Charlotte and across the area. Clouds thicken by daybreak and stay mostly cloudy around Charlotte and the South Carolina Upstate, while western North Carolina clears out during the day. Northeast winds pick up with modest gusts from late morning; around Charlotte the gusts ease from early evening into late tonight, then return early Wednesday morning.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: High pressure over New England wedges cold air against the mountains by Wednesday morning, so Wednesday and Thursday stay chilly, with highs struggling to get out of the 40s. Rain spreads in from the southeast by Wednesday afternoon as a strengthening low-pressure system develops off the Atlantic coast, and it will be cold, rainy and windy from Wednesday afternoon through at least Thursday morning, with a very strong easterly wind just above the ground passing over Wednesday night. Several inches of rain looks likely at a minimum, which on its own would not be a major flooding concern, but if the low tracks farther inland a band of locally heavy rain could set up over the area, and rain falling as fast as 3 inches an hour could cause some flooding. Gusts of at least 30 to 40 mph are expected, with isolated power outages possible, and 40 to 50 mph in the higher-end inland-track scenario; most rain moves out by late Thursday afternoon.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: A brief round of showers, possibly snow showers, could hit the mountains late Thursday into Friday, though confidence is low on how much moisture will be left. Gusty winds continue Thursday night into Friday even as skies dry out. Quiet weather returns for most of the weekend.

watch_for: The storm's track Wednesday into Thursday: a farther-inland path means a heavier rain band, possible flooding and gusts up to 40 to 50 mph.
Wind gusts of 30 to 40 mph Wednesday night into Thursday morning, with isolated power outages possible.
Possible mountain snow showers late Thursday into Friday.
confidence: Confidence is high that a significant storm arrives Wednesday into Thursday but low on exact rainfall amounts and how strong the winds get, which depend on the storm's track; confidence is also low on the Friday mountain showers, while Tuesday and the weekend look quiet.
